title: Buenas
desc: One word does the work of ten

sn.s: Es mi segundo día en Nicaragua.
sn.e: It is my second day in Nicaragua.

sn.s: Salgo de la casa por la mañana.
sn.e: I leave the house in the morning.

sn.s: En la calle hay mucha gente.
sn.e: There are a lot of people in the street.

sn.s: Un señor está en la puerta de su casa.
sn.e: A man is in the doorway of his house.

sn.s: Una señora barre la puerta de su casa.
Yo no digo nada otra vez.
Dos chavalos están en la calle.
sn.e: Two kids are in the street.
A kid walks along with me.
"Why don't you say hello?" he asks me.

sn.s: "¿A toda la gente de la calle?"
sn.e: "To all the people in the street?"
Roberto explains to me how to say hello.

sn.s: Uno saluda al vecino de al lado.
sn.e: You greet the neighbour next door.

sn.s: Uno saluda al vecino de enfrente.
Uno saluda hasta al que no conoce.
sn.e: You even greet the one you do not know.

sn.s: "Saludar no cuesta nada", dice el chavalo.
sn.e: "Saying hello costs nothing," the kid says.

sn.s: Otro chavalo pasa y me saluda.
sn.e: Another kid goes past and greets me.

sn.s: Los chavalos de esta calle saludan a todos.
sn.e: The kids on this street greet everybody.

sn.s: Roberto vive en la casa de al lado.
sn.e: Roberto lives in the house next door.
"And my mum is your neighbour too."

sn.s: Un vecino es el que vive al lado.
sn.e: A neighbour is the one who lives next door.

sn.s: Aquí uno conoce a todos sus vecinos.
sn.e: Here you know all your neighbours.

sn.s: "En la mañana se dice buenos días."
sn.e: "In the morning you say buenos días."

sn.s: "En la tarde se dice buenas tardes."
sn.e: "In the afternoon you say buenas tardes."

sn.s: "En la noche se dice buenas noches."

sn.e: "But you nearly always just say buenas."
"Just buenas and nothing else?" I ask.
We go back down the same street.

sn.s: Los dos chavalos están en la puerta.
sn.e: The two kids are in the doorway.

sn.s: La señora sigue en la puerta de su casa.
sn.e: The woman is still in her doorway.
"Good afternoon, young man," she says to me.

sn.s: El señor está en su puerta.
sn.e: The man is in his doorway.

sn.s: Y ahora la calle es otra calle.
sn.e: And now the street is a different street.

sn.s: La misma gente, la misma calle.
sn.e: The same people, the same street.

sn.s: Pero ahora la gente me habla.
sn.e: But now the people talk to me.

sn.s: Roberto me lleva a su casa.
sn.e: Roberto takes me to his house.

sn.s: En la puerta está su mamá.
sn.e: His mum is in the doorway.

sn.s: "Aquí a las señoras se les dice doña."
"Y a los señores se les dice don."
Doña Carmen me da un vaso de agua.
sn.e: Doña Carmen gives me a glass of water.

sn.s: En la noche pienso en la calle.
sn.e: At night I think about the street.

sn.s: Ayer la gente no me habló.
sn.e: Yesterday the people did not talk to me.
Today the people talked to me.
And I only said one word.
